sampling_model.design: The headline theorems use balanced complete randomization, uniform over assignments with exactly \(n=N/K\) units in each arm. The open kernel problem ranges only over laws in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\): every realized allocation has those fixed counts and every unit has marginal arm probability \(1/K\), without exchangeability.
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) units and all \(K\) potential outcomes per unit are fixed; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object and is generated by the known complete-randomization law or the known admissible nonexchangeable law \(p\).
sampling_model.overlap: Each arm has known marginal assignment probability \(1/K\) and a positive fixed allocation count.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The identification theorem conditions on the armwise empirical marginal laws \(F\); empirical estimation of those margins is outside the first structural kernel and follows the quantile plug-in route of Aronow, Green, and Lee.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The upper bound is attained if the two potential outcomes are comonotonic.
An integer program computes a worst-case copula for broad designs and estimators.
Multi-marginal optimal transport gives exact identified sets for general quadratic cross-world objectives.
The design-based framework permits arbitrary multi-arm contrast matrices.
Supermodular expectations are monotone in concordance for distributions with fixed marginals.
The identity permutation is optimal for a Robinson similarity and dissimilarity when one is Toeplitz.
Isotone imputation converges to a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment.

body.tldr: Under balanced complete randomization, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if the contrast Gram matrix \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. This gives an \(O(K^2)\) certificate, exact six-unit checks, and a binary counterexample outside the cone. Universal Loewner dominance is possible only for a rescaled single pairwise contrast. For arbitrary admissible balanced assignment kernels, an explicit finite cut-product construction now characterizes rank preservation by copositivity and yields exact algebraic certificates and a minimal witness alphabet; polynomial-time recognition remains open.

project_justification.gap: Sharp rank completion is analytic for the two-arm difference-in-means estimator, whereas generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion remains universally least favourable in a multi-arm experiment, nor an exact label-invariant cut characterization restricted to realizable nonexchangeable balanced covariance kernels. The complexity of recognizing that latter feasible-domain cone also remains unsettled.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone for complete randomization, a stronger classification for joint covariance dominance, and a finite copositivity characterization over the exact balanced-law moment polytope modulo common unit relabelling. The finite characterization is exact but is not claimed to be polynomial-time.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete-randomization risk decomposition, proves the graph-Laplacian iff theorem by pairwise rearrangement and isolated binary necessity witnesses, evaluates both mechanisms exactly at \(K=3,N=6\), and classifies the Loewner case. For general balanced kernels it expands ordered columns in cut generators, proves an exact copositivity characterization, gives algebraic yes certificates and rational strict no witnesses, and characterizes the minimal per-arm witness alphabet, while isolating polynomial-time recognition as the remaining open obligation.

body.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee establish the two-arm comonotone sharp endpoint; Proposition 4 recovers that result exactly. Imbens and Menzel use the same isotone completion to obtain a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply the arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance identity used in Lemma 1 but do not optimize its unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular-order theorem covers the classical pairwise rearrangement ingredient, while the proof here gives the required finite swap argument directly. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming. The balanced-kernel extension instead restricts coefficients to the exact finite moment-polytope image of fixed-count, marginally balanced laws and proves a finite copositivity characterization modulo common relabelling. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz quadratic-assignment theorem motivates the cut decomposition but does not provide necessity, feasible-kernel recognition, or the still-open polynomial-time algorithm claimed here only as an open question.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate concerns a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\); it does not turn that scalar endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound. Except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion dominates every linear combination. For a general admissible balanced kernel, the proved recognition procedure enumerates relabellings, arm permutations, supports, and algebraic eigenspace feasibility problems and is therefore factorial/exponential; no polynomial-time algorithm or feasible-domain hardness theorem is established. Binary failure witnesses are complete only when the proved quantity \(L^*(H,\Omega)\) is at most two.
body.honest_scope: The complete-randomization cone theorem follows from the design covariance identity, a finite rearrangement argument, and a new necessity classification; its novelty is the causal contrast geometry and Loewner boundary, not a new general dependence inequality. The \(K=3,N=6\) propositions are exact audit certificates rather than asymptotic claims. On the exact covariance-tensor image of fixed-count, marginally balanced assignment laws, the general extension is proved only to the level of a finite copositivity characterization, exact algebraic yes certificates, rational strict no witnesses, and the minimal finite witness alphabet. The explicit polynomial-time recognition requirement remains open. The project does not claim finite-sample tail dominance, empirical-marginal inference, or a closed form outside the certified complete-randomization cone.
body.interpretation: For complete randomization, checking whether one common-rank completion is least favourable for a prespecified scalar loss requires only checking the off-diagonal signs of \(H\). Joint covariance dominance is much narrower and survives only on one pairwise-contrast ray. Under a nonexchangeable balanced law, rank preservation is still exactly decidable from the design covariance tensor: cut increments turn every possible ordered marginal schedule into a nonnegative vector, and identity-optimality becomes copositivity of finitely many explicit matrices. The current certificate is exact rather than computationally efficient in the worst case.
